key_insight: StochIKM reconstructs multiple plausible individual patient datasets from published Kaplan–Meier curves under explicit fidelity constraints, rather than returning a single reconstruction.
clinical_relevance: The method could support secondary analyses of oncology trial survival outcomes when original patient-level data are unavailable.
method: Uses a vision-capable language model to digitize published Kaplan–Meier figures.
Constrains reconstructions to match risk tables exactly, curves within image resolution, and reported medians, intervals and event counts.
Stochastically generates a set of datasets satisfying these constraints.
evidence_signal: In simulations and 79 published oncology trial arms, StochIKM matched reported risk tables and medians more closely than LLM-improved IPDfromKM.
watch_item: Fidelity depends on correct figure digitization, and admissible reconstructions do not uniquely recover the original patient data.
paper_title: StochIKM: Automated High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Individual Patient Data from Published Kaplan-Meier Curves
